checks.name: a file backs what it said it delivered

must.item: One ~8s vertical video shows fictional adult woman addressing camera at home
must.why: 8 s 9:16 selfie of a woman in her 30s in a living room, looking at camera.

must.item: Complete script audible in English without omissions or additions
must.why: Audio present (peak about -1.5 dB) but not transcribed.

must.item: Readable captions reproduce script exactly and follow speech
must.why: Seen: 'FitTrack makes planning my workouts' at 0.8 s and 'I finally have a routine that sticks.' at 3.2 s. 'so easy.' was not in any sampled frame, and sync can't be checked. They are readable but sit over her mouth.

must.item: Presenter visibly speaks, not a still image
must.why: Mouth shapes change between frames, camera and arm move, and she gestures at the end.

must.item: Ad does not label presenter as verified/real customer

exact_text.text: FitTrack makes planning my workouts so easy. I finally have a routine that sticks.
exact_text.read_as: Captions read 'FitTrack makes planning my workouts' and 'I finally have a routine that sticks.' in sampled frames. 'so easy.' not seen, likely between frames.

faults.what: Captions sit over the presenter's mouth and lower face, which blocks lip movement.
The captions appear to jump straight to the second sentence by 3.2 s, so timing is unverified and 'so easy.' was not visible in any sampled frame.
Two files were delivered (with and without captions), as the assistant said. The assistant also did not check the captions against the script.
Slight AI look and overly smooth skin. No obvious warping or finger errors in the frames.

summary: A convincing 8-second vertical selfie of a fictional woman speaking at home, with readable yellow captions. The caption phrase 'so easy' was not seen and the audio could not be checked; the captions cover her mouth.
